agent_review.notes: All five criteria met on a live cursor-agent turn. The decisive evidence that the answer did NOT come from the screen: the pane's longest line is 119 chars (its wrap width) while the extracted reply's longest line is 201 — the authored line, intact. (1) Both paragraph breaks survive as real blank lines. (2) All three list items begin their own line and keep their '- ' markers; the pane had re-rendered them as the TUI's own '•' glyph, which independently confirms the extraction is transcript-derived rather than screen-derived. (3) No break falls inside a sentence — each paragraph is one unbroken ~200-char line. (4) Directly renderable markdown. (5) Wording, the FMT_ token and punctuation are unchanged. Fingerprint is structural (paragraphs/bullet_lines/unwrapped), not the reply text, because a live model varies its wording between runs and a text fingerprint could never stay approved. Provenance: the FIRST live run of this test legitimately FAILED with wrapped paragraphs and stripped bullets, which is how the markdown-marker gap in llmtypes.sameWords was found — the pane's rendered bullets made an identical message compare as different, so reconciliation fell back to the pane.
